sources.entry: Plik - Scalable and friendly temporary file upload system. (Demo) MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Plik is a self-hosted, scalable temporary file upload system, similar to WeTransfer, with a web interface and command-line client.
summary.what_it_does: Plik lets users upload files through a Vue 3 web interface or a command-line client, then share download links. It supports several storage backends (local disk, S3, OpenStack Swift, Google Cloud Storage) and metadata backends (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL). Uploads can have a configurable TTL with automatic cleanup, be set to OneShot (deleted after the first download), or use stream mode where nothing is stored. Uploads can be password-protected with BasicAuth or end-to-end encrypted with Age, and the CLI and web app can interoperate on encrypted files. Users can also preview files (syntax highlighting, Markdown, Mermaid diagrams, media player), archive files from the CLI or web, and export Prometheus metrics. Authentication providers include Local, Google, GitHub, OVH and OIDC, and an MCP server is available for AI assistant integration.
use_cases: share large files temporarily with others
upload files from the command line with curl
stream files directly from uploader to downloader
how_to_run: wget <release archive URL> && tar xzvf plik-server-1.4.3-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo apt update && sudo apt install plik-server && sudo systemctl start plikd
git clone <repository URL> && cd plik && make && cd server && ./plikd
helm repo add plik <repository URL> && helm install plik plik/plik
notable: Single Go server with a Vue 3 web UI in 12 languages and light, dark and custom themes
Stream mode: data passes from uploader to downloader without being stored
End-to-end encryption with Age, interoperable between CLI and web
Pluggable storage (local, S3, Swift, GCS) and metadata (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL) backends
Includes an MCP server for AI assistant integration
caveats: Some authentication providers (Google, GitHub, OVH, OIDC) require external configuration
Debian/Ubuntu packages and Helm chart are separate install paths that depend on repository setup
